## feec9520847d

**Reproduced contract defects; no source changed.** With seed `17`, sample `0`, difficulty `easy`, and exact controls `run_count=3`, `n_distinct_colors=1`, `palette_size=1`, the generator returned a valid-looking grid containing **five** nonzero colors while `self_check` returned `[]`. The declared `n_distinct_colors` and `palette_size` controls are not consumed. A second exact probe used advertised-valid `grid_h=4`; generation rejected it because the implementation's default branch permits only 7–10. The official lint probe also failed because `RULE_HASH` is absent and reported two diagnostic-axis warnings. Exact overrides, returned grid, source hash `370cf1f9650c6bfab07eefd2168eeaea3a0f4e4d748a79a9fb776236924ee201`, and exception text are retained in `checks/audits/adversarial-probes.json`; lint evidence is under `checks/audits/feec9520847d-lint/`.

**Possible shortcut.** Survivor runs and erased distractors are always drawn from disjoint color pools, so generated lessons never require deciding horizontal-vs-distractor behavior for two objects of the same color. A color-role rule can therefore agree throughout this generator's domain even though color is not semantic in the canonical transformation. I did not construct a Racket-labelled same-color counterexample because this audit was read-only; treat this as a supported distribution concern, not a proved query ambiguity.

triage.reason: Accepted as reviewer-reported source-bound audit evidence. feec9520847d: ignored color controls and advertised dimension rejection; color-role shortcut remains a distribution concern without a Racket-labelled counterexample. 8586bc0f2889: ignored controls, incompatible advertised dimensions and adjacent blob wrongly accepted as markers. Targets unchanged.
